evidence: Most trampers start from the Hacket road-end, 29 km south of Nelson and walk through to Starveall Hut to begin the Alpine Route.
Tarn Hut is located at the edge of a small tarn, to the east of the main ridge, and is reached on a sign-posted access track.
There are two options from Tarn Hut to leave Alpine Route:

evidence: From Tarn Hut, they complete the trip by descending to either Wairoa road-end, inland from Wakefield, or to the Goulter road-end, on the north bank of the Wairau River.
From here, the track leads down the ridge to a sign-posted junction shortly before Bushy Top, with the right-hand track leading to the Wairoa road end.

evidence: At the sign-posted junction shortly before Bushy Top (see above), the left-hand branch leads to the Goulter road end.
The track climbs over Bushy Top (1257 m) before descending down a prominent spur to the Goulter River opposite the Lower Goulter Hut.

doubts: Main way taken as Hacket road end to Tarn Hut (the Alpine Route proper); the two exits from Tarn Hut have their own headings so are W2 and W3. Rintoul Hut has no name entry. Times given only per leg, so null. Wairoa River swingbridge is just downstream of Mid Wairoa Hut. Goulter River crossing is inferred (hut is opposite).
